widget.instructions: Treat both blocks and the string as one body: the pull is the only horizontal external force. Press Play.

stem: Blocks A ({{m1}} kg) and B ({{m2}} kg) on a smooth floor are joined by a light string. A horizontal pull of {{F}} N acts on A, and both move together.

hints.text: The string keeps the blocks together, so they share one acceleration.
Treat A, B and the string as one system. The tension is internal; the only external horizontal force is the pull.

connected-only-one-mass.text: The pull has to accelerate both blocks, because the string drags B along. Use the total mass.

force-times-mass.text: Multiplying gives the wrong units. a = F ÷ total mass.

generic.text: One system, one acceleration: divide the external force by the total mass.

workedSolution.text: System A + B: external horizontal force {{F}} N, total mass {{M}} kg.
a = {{F}} ÷ {{M}} = {{a}} m/s². (The string's tension, {{T}} N, only matters if you look at B alone.)

connected-only-one-mass.front: A pull on A drags B by a string. Which mass sets the acceleration?

force-times-mass.front: Net force F on mass m: acceleration?
force-times-mass.back: a = F ÷ m, not F × m.

generic.front: Connected bodies on a smooth floor?

accessibility.altText: Two blocks, treated as one, with a {{F}} N pull to the right.
accessibility.nonDragAlternative: Press Play to see the motion; type your answer in the box.
